sanskrit: susūkṣmā me samutpannā buddhir dharmārthadarśinī anayā kiṃ mayā kāryaṃ tan me tattvena śaṃsata
english: "A most subtle understanding has arisen in me, one that perceives both dharma and worldly gain. By it, what is it that I must do? Tell me that truly."

sanskrit: yan māṃ bhavanto vakṣyanti kāryam arthasamanvitam tad ahaṃ vai kariṣyāmi nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
english: "Whatever task, sound in purpose, you shall enjoin upon me, that I will surely perform—herein there is no need for hesitation."

sanskrit: tam ūcur atha devās te te caiva paramarṣayaḥ niyato yatra dharmo vai tam aśaṅkaḥ samācara
english: Then those gods and those supreme seers spoke to him: "Wherever dharma stands fixed, that practice without misgiving."

sanskrit: priyāpriye parityajya samaḥ sarveṣu jantuṣu kāmakrodhau ca lobhaṃ ca mānaṃ cotsṛjya dūrataḥ
english: "Casting aside both the pleasing and the unpleasing, even-minded toward all creatures, banishing far from you desire and anger, greed and pride."

sanskrit: yaś ca dharmāt pravicalel loke kaś cana mānavaḥ nigrāhyas te sa bāhubhyāṃ śaśvad dharmam avekṣataḥ
english: "Whatever man in the world should swerve from dharma, he is to be restrained by you with your two arms, you who ever keep your gaze upon dharma."

sanskrit: pratijñāṃ cādhirohasva manasā karmaṇā girā pālayiṣyāmy ahaṃ bhaumaṃ brahma ity eva cāsakṛt
english: "And take this vow in thought, in deed, and in word, again and again: 'I shall protect the sacred order of Brahman upon the earth.'"

sanskrit: yaś cātra dharmanīty ukto daṇḍanītivyapāśrayaḥ tam aśaṅkaḥ kariṣyāmi svavaśo na kadā cana
english: "'And whatever has here been declared the polity of dharma, founded upon the science of just punishment, that I shall carry out without misgiving, never acting at my own caprice.'"

sanskrit: adaṇḍyā me dvijāś ceti pratijānīṣva cābhibho lokaṃ ca saṃkarāt kṛtsnāt trātāsmīti paraṃtapa
english: "And vow, O lord, 'The twice-born are exempt from punishment by me,' and 'I shall guard the world from all confusion of order,' O scorcher of foes."

sanskrit: vainyas tatas tān uvāca devān ṛṣipurogamān brāhmaṇā me sahāyāś ced evam astu surarṣabhāḥ
english: Then the son of Vena said to those gods, led by the seers: "If the brāhmaṇas be my helpers, then so let it be, O bulls among the celestials."

sanskrit: evam astv iti vainyas tu tair ukto brahmavādibhiḥ purodhāś cābhavat tasya śukro brahmamayo nidhiḥ
english: "So be it," the expounders of the Veda said to the son of Vena; and Śukra, that treasure-house full of sacred wisdom, became his household priest.

sanskrit: mantriṇo vālakhilyās tu sārasvatyo gaṇo hy abhūt maharṣir bhagavān gargas tasya sāṃvatsaro 'bhavat
english: The Vālakhilyas were his counselors, and the Sārasvata host became his retinue; the great seer, the venerable Garga, became his astronomer.

sanskrit: ātmanāṣṭama ity eva śrutir eṣā parā nṛṣu utpannau bandinau cāsya tatpūrvau sūtamāgadhau
english: "With himself as the eighth"—such is the high tradition recounted among men; and the first of his bards arose then, the Sūta and the Māgadha.

sanskrit: samatāṃ vasudhāyāś ca sa samyag upapādayat vaiṣamyaṃ hi paraṃ bhūmer āsīd iti ha naḥ śrutam
english: And he brought about, rightly, the levelling of the earth; for great had been the unevenness of the ground before, so we have heard.

sanskrit: sa viṣṇunā ca devena śakreṇa vibudhaiḥ saha ṛṣibhiś ca prajāpālye brahmaṇā cābhiṣecitaḥ
english: He was consecrated to the protection of the people by the god Viṣṇu, by Śakra together with the gods, by the seers, and by Brahmā.

sanskrit: taṃ sākṣāt pṛthivī bheje ratnāny ādāya pāṇḍava sāgaraḥ saritāṃ bhartā himavāṃś cācalottamaḥ
english: The Earth herself, O Pāṇḍava, came to serve him, bearing her jewels, as did the Ocean, lord of rivers, and Himavān, best of mountains.

sanskrit: śakraś ca dhanam akṣayyaṃ prādāt tasya yudhiṣṭhira rukmaṃ cāpi mahāmeruḥ svayaṃ kanakaparvataḥ
english: And Śakra bestowed upon him inexhaustible wealth, O Yudhiṣṭhira, and the great Meru, the golden mountain itself, gave him its gold.

sanskrit: yakṣarākṣasabhartā ca bhagavān naravāhanaḥ dharme cārthe ca kāme ca samarthaṃ pradadau dhanam
english: And the venerable lord of the yakṣas and rākṣasas, he whose mount is a man, gave him wealth sufficient for dharma, for gain, and for pleasure.

sanskrit: hayā rathāś ca nāgāś ca koṭiśaḥ puruṣās tathā prādurbabhūvur vainyasya cintanād eva pāṇḍava na jarā na ca durbhikṣaṃ nādhayo vyādhayas tathā
english: Horses and chariots and elephants, and men by the tens of millions, sprang forth at the mere thought of the son of Vena, O Pāṇḍava; and there was neither old age nor famine, neither anguish of mind nor disease.

sanskrit: sarīsṛpebhyaḥ stenebhyo na cānyonyāt kadā cana bhayam utpadyate tatra tasya rājño 'bhirakṣaṇāt
english: No fear ever arose there—from creeping things, from thieves, nor from one another—because of the protection of that king.

sanskrit: teneyaṃ pṛthivī dugdhā sasyāni daśa sapta ca yakṣarākṣasanāgaiś cāpīpsitaṃ yasya yasya yat
english: By him this Earth was milked of the seventeen kinds of grain, and by the yakṣas, rākṣasas, and nāgas of whatever each of them desired.

sanskrit: tena dharmottaraś cāyaṃ kṛto loko mahātmanā rañjitāś ca prajāḥ sarvās tena rājeti śabdyate
english: By that great-souled one was this world made to abound in dharma, and all his subjects were gladdened by him—therefore is he called rājan.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇānāṃ kṣatatrāṇāt tataḥ kṣatriya ucyate prathitā dhanataś ceyaṃ pṛthivī sādhubhiḥ smṛtā
english: From his shielding the brāhmaṇas from harm he is called kṣatriya; and this Earth, made famous through his wealth, is held by the good to be Pṛthivī.

sanskrit: sthāpanaṃ cākarod viṣṇuḥ svayam eva sanātanaḥ nātivartiṣyate kaś cid rājaṃs tvām iti pārthiva
english: And Viṣṇu, the eternal, himself made this ordinance: "No one shall ever transgress against you, O king," O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: tapasā bhagavān viṣṇur āviveśa ca bhūmipam devavan naradevānāṃ namate yaj jagan nṛpa
english: And by his ascetic power the venerable Viṣṇu entered into that lord of the earth; therefore the world bows before kings as before a god, O king.

sanskrit: daṇḍanītyā ca satataṃ rakṣitaṃ taṃ nareśvara nādharṣayat tataḥ kaś cic cāranityāc ca darśanāt
english: Guarded ever by the science of just rule, O lord of men, no one could assail him—and because of his constant watch through spies and his vigilance, none dared.

sanskrit: ātmanā karaṇaiś caiva samasyeha mahīkṣitaḥ ko hetur yad vaśe tiṣṭhel loko daivād ṛte guṇāt
english: When the king is the equal of any other in his own person and in his instruments of rule, what cause is there that the world should remain in his power, save divine ordinance and his innate worth?

sanskrit: viṣṇor lalāṭāt kamalaṃ sauvarṇam abhavat tadā śrīḥ saṃbhūtā yato devī patnī dharmasya dhīmataḥ
english: From the brow of Viṣṇu there arose then a golden lotus, whence was born the goddess Śrī, the wife of wise Dharma.

sanskrit: śriyaḥ sakāśād arthaś ca jāto dharmeṇa pāṇḍava atha dharmas tathaivārthaḥ śrīś ca rājye pratiṣṭhitā
english: And from Śrī, Artha was born through Dharma, O Pāṇḍava; thus Dharma, and likewise Artha, and Śrī, are established in kingship.

sanskrit: sukṛtasya kṣayāc caiva svarlokād etya medinīm pārthivo jāyate tāta daṇḍanītivaśānugaḥ
english: And through the spending of his merit, having descended from heaven to the earth, a man is born a king, my son, subject to the rule of just punishment.

sanskrit: mahattvena ca saṃyukto vaiṣṇavena naro bhuvi buddhyā bhavati saṃyukto māhātmyaṃ cādhigacchati
english: Endowed upon the earth with that greatness which is of Viṣṇu, such a man becomes endowed with wisdom and attains to majesty of soul.

sanskrit: sthāpanām atha devānāṃ na kaś cid ativartate tiṣṭhaty ekasya ca vaśe taṃ ced anuvidhīyate
english: This ordinance of the gods none transgresses; and the world abides in the power of one alone, if it is governed accordingly.

sanskrit: śubhaṃ hi karma rājendra śubhatvāyopakalpate tulyasyaikasya yasyāyaṃ loko vacasi tiṣṭhati
english: For an auspicious deed, O lord of kings, conduces to weal—that of the one man, though the equal of others, in whose word this world abides.

sanskrit: yo hy asya mukham adrākṣīt somya so 'sya vaśānugaḥ subhagaṃ cārthavantaṃ ca rūpavantaṃ ca paśyati
english: For whoever has looked upon his face, gentle one, becomes obedient to his will, beholding it as gracious, full of meaning, and fair of form.

sanskrit: tato jagati rājendra satataṃ śabditaṃ budhaiḥ devāś ca naradevāś ca tulyā iti viśāṃ pate
english: Therefore in the world, O lord of kings, it has ever been proclaimed by the wise: "The gods and the gods among men are equal," O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ mahattvaṃ prati rājasu kārtsnyena bharataśreṣṭha kim anyad iha vartatām
english: All this concerning the greatness that resides in kings has now been related to you in full, O best of the Bharatas. What else shall be set forth here?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ punaḥ sa gāṅgeyam abhivādya pitāmaham prāñjalir niyato bhūtvā paryapṛcchad yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then once more, having saluted the grandsire, the son of Gaṅgā, and having become composed with palms joined, Yudhiṣṭhira put his question.

sanskrit: ke dharmāḥ sarvavarṇānāṃ cāturvarṇyasya ke pṛthak caturṇām āśramāṇāṃ ca rājadharmāś ca ke matāḥ
english: "What are the duties common to all the orders, and what severally are those of the four castes? What are held to be the duties of the four stages of life, and what the duties of a king?"

sanskrit: kena svid vardhate rāṣṭraṃ rājā kena vivardhate kena paurāś ca bhṛtyāś ca vardhante bharatarṣabha
english: "By what does a realm prosper, by what does a king grow great, and by what do the citizens and the retainers flourish, O bull of the Bharatas?"

sanskrit: kośaṃ daṇḍaṃ ca durgaṃ ca sahāyān mantriṇas tathā ṛtvikpurohitācāryān kīdṛśān varjayen nṛpaḥ
english: "As for treasury, army, and fortress, and allies and counselors, as well as officiating priests, household priests, and teachers—what manner of men should a king shun?"

sanskrit: keṣu viśvasitavyaṃ syād rājñāṃ kasyāṃ cid āpadi kuto vātmā dṛḍho rakṣyas tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: "In whom should kings place their trust in any calamity, and against what should one's own self be firmly guarded? Tell me that, O grandsire."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca namo dharmāya mahate namaḥ kṛṣṇāya vedhase brāhmaṇebhyo namaskṛtvā dharmān vakṣyāmi śāśvatān
english: Bhīṣma said: Homage to mighty Dharma, homage to Kṛṣṇa the ordainer! Having made obeisance to the brāhmaṇas, I shall declare the eternal duties.

sanskrit: akrodhaḥ satyavacanaṃ saṃvibhāgaḥ kṣamā tathā prajanaḥ sveṣu dāreṣu śaucam adroha eva ca
english: Freedom from anger, truthful speech, fair sharing, and forbearance; the begetting of offspring upon one's own wife, purity, and freedom from malice.

sanskrit: ārjavaṃ bhṛtyabharaṇaṃ navaite sārvavarṇikāḥ brāhmaṇasya tu yo dharmas taṃ te vakṣyāmi kevalam
english: Uprightness, and the maintenance of those who depend upon one—these nine belong to all the castes alike. But the duty that is the brāhmaṇa's alone, that I shall now declare to you.

sanskrit: damam eva mahārāja dharmam āhuḥ purātanam svādhyāyo 'dhyāpanaṃ caiva tatra karma samāpyate
english: Self-restraint, O great king, the ancients declared to be the foremost duty; in the study of the Veda and the teaching of it, the brāhmaṇa's work is fulfilled.

sanskrit: taṃ ced vittam upāgacched vartamānaṃ svakarmaṇi akurvāṇaṃ vikarmāṇi śāntaṃ prajñānatarpitam
english: Should wealth come to such a one, while he abides in his own proper work, doing no forbidden deeds, tranquil, and contented in the satisfaction of wisdom—

sanskrit: kurvītāpatyasaṃtānam atho dadyād yajeta ca saṃvibhajya hi bhoktavyaṃ dhanaṃ sadbhir itīṣyate
english: let him beget a line of offspring, and then give gifts and offer sacrifice; for it is held by the good that wealth should be enjoyed only when it has been shared out.

sanskrit: pariniṣṭhitakāryas tu svādhyāyenaiva brāhmaṇaḥ kuryād anyan na vā kuryān maitro brāhmaṇa ucyate
english: But the brāhmaṇa who has accomplished his task through the study of the Veda alone may do other works or may not; he, being friendly to all, is called a true brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: kṣatriyasyāpi yo dharmas taṃ te vakṣyāmi bhārata dadyād rājā na yāceta yajeta na tu yājayet
english: The duty that belongs to the kṣatriya also I shall declare to you, O Bhārata: a king should give but not beg, should sacrifice but not officiate as priest for others.

sanskrit: nādhyāpayed adhīyīta prajāś ca paripālayet nityodyukto dasyuvadhe raṇe kuryāt parākramam
english: He should not teach, but should study; he should protect his subjects; ever ready for the slaying of marauders, he should show his valor in battle.

sanskrit: ye ca kratubhir ījānāḥ śrutavantaś ca bhūmipāḥ ya evāhavajetāras ta eṣāṃ lokajittamāḥ
english: Of those rulers who have offered sacrifices and are learned in the Veda, those very ones who are conquerors in battle are the foremost winners of worlds.

sanskrit: avikṣatena dehena samarād yo nivartate kṣatriyo nāsya tat karma praśaṃsanti purāvidaḥ
english: The kṣatriya who returns from battle with his body unwounded—those versed in the ancient lore do not praise that deed of his.

sanskrit: vadhaṃ hi kṣatrabandhūnāṃ dharmam āhuḥ pradhānataḥ nāsya kṛtyatamaṃ kiṃ cid anyad dasyunibarhaṇāt
english: For the slaying of the foes of the kṣatra-order is declared to be his foremost duty; there is no act more fitting for him than the crushing of marauders.

sanskrit: dānam adhyayanaṃ yajño yogaḥ kṣemo vidhīyate tasmād rājñā viśeṣeṇa yoddhavyaṃ dharmam īpsatā
english: Giving, study, sacrifice, the practice of yoga, and the securing of welfare are enjoined upon him; therefore a king who seeks dharma must above all be ready to fight.

sanskrit: sveṣu dharmeṣv avasthāpya prajāḥ sarvā mahīpatiḥ dharmeṇa sarvakṛtyāni samaniṣṭhāni kārayet
english: Having established all his subjects each in their own duties, the lord of the earth should cause all their undertakings to be brought to fulfillment in accordance with dharma.

sanskrit: pariniṣṭhitakāryaḥ syān nṛpatiḥ paripālanāt kuryād anyan na vā kuryād aindro rājanya ucyate
english: A king may be deemed to have accomplished his task through the protecting of his people; he may do other works or may not, and is then called a prince of Indra's stamp.

sanskrit: vaiśyasyāpīha yo dharmas taṃ te vakṣyāmi bhārata dānam adhyayanaṃ yajñaḥ śaucena dhanasaṃcayaḥ
english: The duty that here belongs to the vaiśya also I shall declare to you, O Bhārata: giving, study, sacrifice, and the gathering of wealth by honest means.

sanskrit: pitṛvat pālayed vaiśyo yuktaḥ sarvapaśūn iha vikarma tad bhaved anyat karma yad yat samācaret rakṣayā sa hi teṣāṃ vai mahat sukham avāpnuyāt
english: Diligent, the vaiśya should tend all his cattle here as a father tends his children; any other work that he should undertake would be a forbidden deed for him; for by guarding them he shall indeed attain great happiness.

sanskrit: prajāpatir hi vaiśyāya sṛṣṭvā paridade paśūn brāhmaṇāya ca rājñe ca sarvāḥ paridade prajāḥ
english: For Prajāpati, having created the cattle, made them over to the vaiśya, while to the brāhmaṇa and to the king he made over all the people.

sanskrit: tasya vṛttiṃ pravakṣyāmi yac ca tasyopajīvanam ṣaṇṇām ekāṃ pibed dhenuṃ śatāc ca mithunaṃ haret
english: I shall declare his means of living and that whereby he sustains himself: of six cows he may take the milk of one, and from a hundred he may take a pair.

sanskrit: laye ca saptamo bhāgas tathā śṛṅge kalā khure sasyasya sarvabījānām eṣā sāṃvatsarī bhṛtiḥ
english: On the produce a seventh part, and likewise a small share on horn and hoof; and of grain and of all seeds—this is his yearly maintenance.

sanskrit: na ca vaiśyasya kāmaḥ syān na rakṣeyaṃ paśūn iti vaiśye cecchati nānyena rakṣitavyāḥ kathaṃ cana
english: And it must never be the vaiśya's wish to say, "I will not guard the cattle"; and if the vaiśya is willing, they are by no means to be guarded by any other.

sanskrit: śūdrasyāpi hi yo dharmas taṃ te vakṣyāmi bhārata prajāpatir hi varṇānāṃ dāsaṃ śūdram akalpayat
english: The duty that belongs to the śūdra also I shall declare to you, O Bhārata: Prajāpati appointed the śūdra to be the servant of the castes.

sanskrit: tasmāc chūdrasya varṇānāṃ paricaryā vidhīyate teṣāṃ śuśrūṣaṇāc caiva mahat sukham avāpnuyāt
english: Therefore service to the castes is enjoined upon the śūdra; and by his ministering to them he shall attain great happiness.

sanskrit: śūdra etān paricaret trīn varṇān anasūyakaḥ saṃcayāṃś ca na kurvīta jātu śūdraḥ kathaṃ cana
english: Let the śūdra serve these three castes without spite; and let the śūdra never in any way make hoardings of wealth.

sanskrit: pāpīyān hi dhanaṃ labdhvā vaśe kuryād garīyasaḥ rājñā vā samanujñātaḥ kāmaṃ kurvīta dhārmikaḥ
english: For a baser man, having gained wealth, would bring his betters under his sway; but if permitted by the king, a righteous one may do so at his pleasure.

sanskrit: tasya vṛttiṃ pravakṣyāmi yac ca tasyopajīvanam avaśyabharaṇīyo hi varṇānāṃ śūdra ucyate
english: I shall declare his means of living and that whereby he sustains himself; for the śūdra is said to be one whom the castes are bound to maintain.

sanskrit: chatraṃ veṣṭanam auśīram upānad vyajanāni ca yātayāmāni deyāni śūdrāya paricāriṇe
english: An umbrella, a turban, a mat of fragrant grass, sandals, and fans—worn or used articles such as these are to be given to the śūdra who serves.

sanskrit: adhāryāṇi viśīrṇāni vasanāni dvijātibhiḥ śūdrāyaiva vidheyāni tasya dharmadhanaṃ hi tat
english: Garments that have become unfit to wear and are worn out by the twice-born are to be assigned to the śūdra alone; for that is his rightful portion.

sanskrit: yaś ca kaś cid dvijātīnāṃ śūdraḥ śuśrūṣur āvrajet kalpyāṃ tasya tu tenāhur vṛttiṃ dharmavido janāḥ deyaḥ piṇḍo 'napetāya bhartavyau vṛddhadurbalau
english: And whatever śūdra should come willing to serve among the twice-born, by that one his fitting maintenance is to be provided, so say those who know dharma; a portion of food is to be given to the one who does not forsake his master, and the aged and the feeble among such are to be supported.

sanskrit: śūdreṇa ca na hātavyo bhartā kasyāṃ cid āpadi atirekeṇa bhartavyo bhartā dravyaparikṣaye na hi svam asti śūdrasya bhartṛhāryadhano hy asau
english: And the master must not be abandoned by the śūdra in any calamity; rather, when the master's substance is exhausted, he must be supported all the more, for the śūdra has no property of his own, since his wealth is such as the master may rightfully take.

sanskrit: uktas trayāṇāṃ varṇānāṃ yajñas trayyaiva bhārata svāhākāranamaskārau mantraḥ śūdre vidhīyate
english: For the three castes the sacrifice has been declared to be by means of the threefold Veda, O Bhārata; but for the śūdra the sacred utterance is enjoined to be the cry of svāhā and the reverential salutation.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ śūdraḥ pākayajñair yajeta vratavān svayam pūrṇapātramayīm āhuḥ pākayajñasya dakṣiṇām
english: With these two the śūdra, keeping his vows, may himself sacrifice by means of the simple cooked-food offerings; the sacrificial fee for such an offering, they say, consists of a vessel filled with food.

sanskrit: śūdraḥ paijavano nāma sahasrāṇāṃ śataṃ dadau aindrāgnena vidhānena dakṣiṇām iti naḥ śrutam
english: A śūdra named Paijavana gave a hundred thousand as the sacrificial fee, according to the rite of Indra and Agni—so have we heard.

sanskrit: ato hi sarvavarṇānāṃ śraddhāyajño vidhīyate daivataṃ hi mahac chraddhā pavitraṃ yajatāṃ ca yat
english: Hence for all the castes the sacrifice of faith is enjoined; for faith is a great divinity, and it is that which sanctifies those who sacrifice.

sanskrit: daivataṃ paramaṃ viprāḥ svena svena parasparam ayajann iha satrais te tais taiḥ kāmaiḥ sanātanaiḥ
english: The supreme divinity the brāhmaṇas worshipped here, each by his own rite and among one another, with their long sacrificial sessions and with those several eternal desires.

sanskrit: saṃsṛṣṭā brāhmaṇair eva triṣu varṇeṣu sṛṣṭayaḥ devānām api ye devā yad brūyus te paraṃ hi tat tasmād varṇaiḥ sarvayajñāḥ saṃsṛjyante na kāmyayā
english: By the brāhmaṇas alone were the creations of the three castes brought forth; and they who are gods even of the gods—whatsoever they should pronounce, that indeed is supreme; therefore all sacrifices are brought about through the castes, not by self-interested desire.

sanskrit: ṛgyajuḥsāmavit pūjyo nityaṃ syād devavad dvijaḥ anṛgyajur asāmā tu prājāpatya upadravaḥ
english: A twice-born one who knows the Ṛk, the Yajus, and the Sāman should ever be honored like a god; but he who lacks the Ṛk, the Yajus, and the Sāman is a blight upon the realm of Prajāpati.

sanskrit: yajño manīṣayā tāta sarvavarṇeṣu bhārata nāsya yajñahano devā īhante netare janāḥ tasmāt sarveṣu varṇeṣu śraddhāyajño vidhīyate
english: Sacrifice springs from devout intent, my son, among all the castes, O Bhārata; the gods do not strive after the sacrifice of one who destroys it, nor do other men; therefore among all the castes the sacrifice of faith is enjoined.

sanskrit: svaṃ daivataṃ brāhmaṇāḥ svena nityaṃ; parān varṇān ayajann evam āsīt ārocitā naḥ sumahān sa dharmaḥ; sṛṣṭo brahmaṇā triṣu varṇeṣu dṛṣṭaḥ
english: The brāhmaṇas ever worshipped their own divinity by their own rite, and so they caused the other castes to sacrifice; thus it was. That mighty law has been made known to us, ordained by Brahmā and beheld among the three castes.

sanskrit: tasmād varṇā ṛjavo jātidharmāḥ; saṃsṛjyante tasya vipāka eṣaḥ ekaṃ sāma yajur ekam ṛg ekā; vipraś caiko 'niścayas teṣu dṛṣṭaḥ
english: Hence the castes are upright in their inborn duties; they are brought forth in due order, and this is the ripening of that ordinance: one is the Sāman, one the Yajus, and one the Ṛk, and one is the brāhmaṇa—yet among these an uncertainty has been observed.
